summary: An old version of the IMP and TIP preventive maintenance schedule, replaced by RFC 638.

eli5.summary: A schedule for when network boxes get serviced. A corrected one replaced it.

subtitle: Schedule of preventive maintenance windows for all IMP and TIP machines.

tldr.problem: ARPANET users needed to know when each site's packet-switching machine would be unavailable for regular maintenance.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 633 publishes a monthly schedule of preventive maintenance (PM) times for every IMP and TIP on the network, grouped by week of the month and listed with the site name and the Eastern Time window.
tldr.outcome: The schedule lets users and system operators plan around known downtime, though the RFC notes that unexpected rescheduling may be necessary.

today: RFC 633 is a historic maintenance schedule. It was superseded by RFC 638.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: RFC 633 presents the preventive maintenance schedule for every IMP (Interface Message Processor) and TIP (Terminal Interface Processor) on ARPANET. Preventive maintenance is scheduled monthly, with each machine assigned a consistent time of the month. Where possible, the PM window aligns with the host's own maintenance time to minimize disruption.
sections.eli5: All the packet routers get monthly check-ups. Each one has its own day and time.

sections.title: The Schedule
sections.content: The schedule is organized by week of month (first through fourth) and then by day (Monday through Friday). Each entry lists the site name and the maintenance window in Eastern Time (e.g., "BBN IMP [0830-1130]"). Most PMs do not require the machine to be down, but users should not rely on the machine remaining available during the PM period. Tuesday mornings from 7 to 9 am are always reserved for network-wide software maintenance.
sections.eli5: The schedule says which day each machine gets serviced and from when to when, in Eastern Time. Don't count on the network working during these windows.

sections.title: Rescheduling and Contingencies
sections.content: The RFC notes that PM scheduling sometimes must change due to network connectivity considerations or other reasons. When rescheduling is necessary, BBN follows the usual procedure for scheduling downtime with the site's primary contact. Permanent changes to the schedule are announced via RFC.
sections.eli5: If the schedule needs to change, BBN calls the site first and posts an updated schedule.
